title: Ang 792–794: Suhi's Bhagats
hook: Kabir, Ravidas and Farid, who says you didn't build the raft when you could (ang 794)
tomorrow: why would calling a sultan 'chief' be a small compliment?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Suhi ki Var: faithful, moved off the funeral fire and into each morning. Today the Bhagats close the raga, and one of them asks about a raft.

Group projects have a pattern. The week everyone says "we've got time" is the week that decides everything. Farid, a Sufi poet whose verses sit in the Granth, writes about that week. On ang 794 he says: you couldn't build your raft when it was time to build it. Here's the odd part. The lake in his poem is already overflowing. So why is he scolding someone about a raft, instead of throwing them a rope?
screen: `"WE'VE GOT TIME."` → `THE RAFT NOBODY BUILT.` → `WHY SCOLD, NOT THROW A ROPE?`

segments.voice: Suhi's last pages belong to the Bhagats. Kabir comes first. Then Ravidas, who sings that the happy bride is the one who knows her Husband's worth. Then Farid, with two hymns. The second holds the raft. In paraphrase: you couldn't bind your raft together when it was time to bind it. When the lake is full and its waves leap up, crossing is hard. Then a warning: don't touch the safflower, beloved; its color will burn away. So, the puzzle. Why scold instead of rescue? Because Farid isn't really talking to someone in the flood. He's talking to the listener, who still has dry ground. The poem is set at the hard moment so you can hear it at the easy one. A raft is built in calm water, plank by plank. For Farid, the planks are the habits of love and remembering, made while life is quiet. The safflower fits too: a bright dye that looks wonderful and fades. And the hymn ends soberly. In paraphrase: says Farid, friends, the Husband will call; the swan will fly off, and this body will become a heap of dust. Here's the thing worth telling a friend: a Sufi's poem about a raft sits in the Sikh scripture, and its advice is plain. Not when the water rises. Now.
screen: `KABIR, RAVIDAS, THEN FARID.` · `BUILD THE RAFT IN CALM WATER.` · `SAFFLOWER: BRIGHT, AND IT FADES.` · `THE SWAN WILL FLY.` · then, large: `BUILD THE RAFT NOW.`

segments.voice: Name one thing you'd want ready for a rough season: a friendship, a habit, a skill. Name what keeps pushing it to "later." Then pick one plank you could lay this week, and hold that small plan quietly for the sit. If you'd like, read Farid's raft on ang 794 first.
Ang 792. Where Suhi's Bhagats begin: Kabir, Ravidas, and Farid with his raft, closing the raga.
Build the raft now, plank by plank, while the water is still calm. Suhi ends on that.

howItsDone: Sheikh Farid's hymns are sung in kirtan in their raga like the Gurus' own; his raft verse in Suhi, on ang 794, comes just before raga Bilaval begins.

fork.setup: your cousin wants to learn bebe's dal 'someday, when things slow down.' bebe still cooks it every sunday. what does Farid's raft say?
options: learn it this sunday, while she's there to teach it.
wait until she offers; asking now would be pushy.
look up a recipe online; it's the same thing.
fork.reveal: build it in calm water: the raft is made before the lake rises, not when it does.

chat.meaning: Farid: the raft is built before the lake overflows. Waiting for a calmer moment is how the crossing gets hard.
